skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: +1 headless, and the count is the least of it: 171 OF 208 HEADLESS FACTS COULD LEAK A LIVE APPLICATION HOST INTO THE NEXT TEST (unit unchanged at 3020). THE EXTENT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is why the fix is a harness change and not a patch: 188 facts construct an ApplicationHost; 17 already wrapped it in try/finally; the other 171 had `await host.ShutdownAsync()` as their LAST STATEMENT, unreachable through a throw. SEVEN WERE WORSE THAN EXPOSED and leaked on GREEN runs too - GoonPracticeHeadlessTests (4) boots a host and never shuts it down, RackPresentationAnchorHeadlessTests (3) discards the host entirely. WHY THIS MATTERED EVEN THOUGH IT ONLY SURFACED UNDER A MUTATION: a failing fact could corrupt the one after it, so a single genuine failure could cascade into misleading ones and send whoever read the run at the wrong defect. This suite is the port's evidence base; a run that misreports WHICH fact broke is worse than a slow one. THE SHAPE WAS CHOSEN AGAINST FOUR NAMED ALTERNATIVES: a class fixture is the wrong LIFETIME (every fact boots its own host against its own temp data root, and sharing one changes what the facts test); `await using` on the boot record needs 188 call sites restructured because of deconstruction; try/finally in each of the 171 is ~3000 re-indented lines for a property that belongs to the harness, and the next fact anyone writes forgets it again; an ambient static collector is wrong under per-class parallelism. Instance scope IS per-fact scope - xunit builds a fresh test-class instance per fact and disposes it whatever the outcome - and the base ASSERTS rather than assumes that disposal lands on the dispatcher thread, because AvaloniaTestRunner overrides the whole per-test Run; 209 of 209 pass through that assertion. THE DEMONSTRATION LEAVES NO RED BEHIND, and how is the interesting part: the throwing type is real and test-class-shaped - it boots a real host through the real composition root, starts a real scripted session, and fails an assertion exactly where the mutation made a real fact fail - but it CARRIES NO FACT ATTRIBUTE, so xunit never schedules it. `Assert.Fail` returns void, so the trailing shutdown is reachable-but-unreached and needs no #pragma, which would itself have tripped the warning-suppression census. THE RUNNER HALF WAS MEASURED OUT OF BAND WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL and then deleted: a genuinely red fact gave Total 210 / Failed 1, that one BY NAME with NO CASCADE, and its teardown lines followed its last log line; with the Track call removed, nothing followed. That isolates the mechanism. NOT PROVED: the original cascade was never reproduced - the leak and its removal are proved, but the causal chain from leak to that specific misreport remains the board's account rather than a measurement; windows that a fact Shows are still never Closed, on any path, and extending teardown to close them would be a behaviour change wearing a harness change's clothes; and the permanent fact invokes DisposeAsync directly rather than exercising xunit's own call. CcpClient.HeadlessTests 208 to 209.
